content:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - Third-party auth verification errors detected for /verify endpoint (AuthZero). High 5xx / timeouts starting ~15:12 UTC. Paging @maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): seeing spikes in 5xxs from auth-proxy (auth-verify). Users hitting login loops and console access failing. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/auth-verify

kevin: logs show upstream https://authz.prod/verify returning 502/504 and long tails (~20s). Our retry loop is amplifying load -> connection pool exhaustion on auth-proxy.

jess: support queue: 48 tickets so far, several enterprise tenants cannot sign in. Error surfaced as TOKEN_VERIFICATION_FAILED in client.

sam: getting stack traces from auth-proxy: 
```
ERR upstream timeout after 15000ms
at auth-proxy/verify (verify_client.go:142)
```

maria (oncall): mitigation options: 1) enable local tolerant cache on auth-proxy 2) degrade upstream concurrency / fast-fail 3) route a portion of traffic to backup auth endpoint 4) notify vendor SRE. I'll start with 1 + 3.

sam: enabling local-cache now (accept cached tokens for short TTL) to avoid immediate failures while upstream recovers.

opsbot: command: /service auth-proxy toggle-local-cache --enable --ttl=60

opsbot: response: OK - local-cache enabled on 8 instances; rolling restart initiated.

kevin: applying fast-fail circuit for /verify at ingress to avoid thread exhaustion. Changing nginx upstream_timeout to 3s and reducing retries.

opsbot: command: /infra config apply ingress-nginx --set upstream.timeout=3s --set upstream.retries=1

opsbot: response: rollout started, new config applied to 5 ingresses.

maria (oncall): routing 10% of traffic to backup endpoint in us-west-2 to relieve pressure.

opsbot: command: /router set-route auth-verify upstream=authz-uswest2.example.com --weight=10

opsbot: response: route update applied. us-west-2 receiving 10% of traffic.

kevin: error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~5% within 4m after route + cache. Latency on backup ~200ms. Looks promising.

jess: drafted status page update: "We are investigating authentication errors affecting sign-in and console access. Mitigations are in progress." Shall I publish? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria (oncall): publish and mention enterprise customers will be contacted by support.

jess: published at 15:20 UTC.

sam: note from logs: our clients were retrying aggressively (no jitter) leading to TCP TIME_WAIT and fd exhaustion on auth-proxy. Backup route reduced pressure. Recommend client retry/backoff + jitter in next deploy.

maria (oncall): handing off to kevin for the next shift at 16:00 UTC. Handoff notes: local-cache ttl=60, ingress fast-fail timeout=3s, backup route weight=10%. Monitor cache hit-rate and error count.

kevin: taking over. Will keep thread active and escalate to vendor if error rate >10% for >15m. Assigning post-incident owner and RCA.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: P1 - auth-thirdparty-degradation; start_ts=1892345678.

jess: support created customer tickets for affected tenants: RDW-2134, RDW-2135, RDW-2140. Notifying CSMs for top accounts.

maria (oncall): action items: - open vendor ticket with AuthZero with logs and timeline - implement client retry jitter + lower retry count in next patch - evaluate increasing cache TTL to 300s for dedicated customers - postmortem owner: kevin (eng-sre)

kevin: assigned. I will draft the postmortem and run RCA within 24h. Will include timeline of rolling restarts, routing changes, and config diffs.

jess: closing the bridge, leaving thread open for vendor response and final recovery confirmation.

support: update: triaged top enterprise tenants, providing interim workarounds and monitoring.

kevin: final check at 15:55 UTC -> error rate steady ~2.3% after increasing backup weight to 30%. Partial recovery achieved, continuing to monitor.

sam: quick follow-up: add jitter and cap retries at 2 for verification calls. I'll open a change PR now.

maria (oncall): thanks team. I'll mark this as partially mitigated; keep thread for follow-ups.
